title: Get feedback on your practice work
summary: Practice only improves with feedback. Ask people who do the job to review your work against what good looks like, then change something.

beginner: Choose the criteria you want feedback on, using a published framework as a guide. The government product manager skills in the sources are a good start: for example user focus, evidence, prioritisation and communication.
Ask two product managers or colleagues you met earlier to read your case study and answer three questions: what is strongest, what is weakest or unclear, and what would you expect to see next.
Offer to return the favour, and keep the request small: fifteen minutes of reading and a short reply.
Listen without defending. Write down what you heard in their words, then decide what to change and what to keep, with a reason for each.
Make at least one visible change and record it as a 'before and after'.
Thank them and tell them what you changed.

toolExamples.notion: Keep a table of feedback, what you decided and why.

definitionOfDone: Feedback from two people on stated criteria
At least one visible change made
pitfalls: Asking 'what do you think?' with no focus
